title: ProgramKit Development Tools
intent: Define a provider-neutral executable Development Tool identity and contract, prove it through an exact generated Console tool, and add one human-started, digest-locked Codex MCP registration lifecycle without granting autonomous authority.
scope: A versioned manifest for exact tool package, executable, operations, schemas, exit codes, permissions, side effects, timeouts, cancellation, concurrency, idempotency, compatibility, evidence, and documentation ownership.
A package-only generated Console proof tool using current ProgramKit Console generation source truth.
A thin Codex adapter over stable MCP standard input/output revision 2025-11-25.
Explicit collision-safe Codex registration, verification, update, and removal.
A genuine two-session cold-discovery proof and negative fixtures.
nonGoals: Implementation, registration, permissions, an MCP server, provider binding, capability, plugin, autonomous loop, package publication, release, deployment, or website authority under design approval.
Any consumer use of ProgramKit project references, source/file includes, assembly hint paths, or build outputs.
assumptions: Current Codex project-scoped MCP configuration and stable MCP 2025-11-25 remain authoritative at implementation start; material drift stops implementation for renewed review.
The current generated Console dispatcher and one-shot lifecycle are the source truth for the first proof tool.
A trusted project can persist the reviewed .codex/config.toml server table between completely separate Codex sessions.
Locally prepared NuGet packages and controlled package-source mapping are available and remain the only ProgramKit consumer boundary.

unresolvedDecisions.question: Do the authoritative Codex MCP configuration and stable MCP contracts still support the exact reviewed adapter and registration at implementation start?
unresolvedDecisions.blockingEffect: Material drift blocks adapter and registration implementation and requires renewed design review.

sourceTruthAuthorities.governs: Exact identities, invocation and registration semantics, transport decision, cold-session proof, package boundary, exclusions, and approval boundary.
Current generated Console parse, dispatcher, lifecycle, cancellation-carrier, and exact integer exit-result behavior used by the proof.
Current backed command composition, local package preparation, local publish, and capability boundaries; unbacked render, graph, and check commands are not treated as available.

domains.purpose: Own explicit, inspectable executable development-tool contracts and provider registration evidence without owning AI authority or consumer-domain behavior.

vocabulary.meaning: An exact versioned package and executable exposing schema-governed operations under declared permissions, side effects, execution semantics, and compatibility.
A thin reviewed transport projection that discovers and invokes one exact provider-neutral tool contract without adding domain meaning or authority.
Discovery and invocation in a new provider session solely from persisted reviewed registration, with no inherited conversational, command, path, process, or shell state.

semanticModels.meaning: Exact package, executable, operation schema, execution, access, compatibility, evidence, and documentation facts required before a tool can be invoked or advertised.
semanticModels.invariants: Every referenced package, executable, schema, and adapter byte is digest-bound; access is denied unless declared; stdout is one schema-valid result; retry and concurrency never exceed the manifest.

semanticModels.meaning: Ownership proof for one exact Codex project-scoped MCP server table and the exact package, contract, executable, and adapter bytes it exposes.
semanticModels.invariants: Registration, update, and removal are explicit; collision and drift fail closed; unrelated TOML remains unowned and unchanged; removal deletes only exactly owned state.

components.compatibilityBoundary: Contract/schema identity, manifest fields, exit-code profile, permission and side-effect enum, canonical serialization, and explicit migrations.

components.purpose: Demonstrate the contract with a generated Console application consuming ProgramKit only through exact prepared packages.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Orbyss.ProgramKit.DevelopmentTool.ConsoleProof@0.1.0-alpha.1, executable program-kit-development-tool-console-proof, exact manifest/schema digests, and current generated Console dispatcher behavior.

components.purpose: Project one exact provider-neutral tool as one stable MCP 2025-11-25 stdio server/tool and enforce the reviewed invocation policy.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Orbyss.ProgramKit.DevelopmentTool.Adapter.Codex.Mcp@0.1.0-alpha.1, executable program-kit-development-tool-codex-mcp, server id program_kit_console_proof, tool name program-kit.console-proof.invoke, stable MCP revision, and authoritative Codex config keys.

components.purpose: Verify exact bytes and explicitly register, update, remove, and audit only the owned project-scoped Codex MCP table.
components.compatibilityBoundary: Collision refusal, normalized owned-table digest, exact lock ownership, TOML preservation, human-started commands, and non-discovery after removal.

referenceRules.referencingScope: Console proof tool, Codex adapter, and cold-session fixture applications
referenceRules.referencedScope: ProgramKit projects, source/file includes, assembly hint paths, and ProgramKit build outputs
referenceRules.rationale: All consumers must restore exact locally prepared packages through controlled NuGet source mapping.

referenceRules.referencingScope: Development Tool executable and provider adapter runtime
referenceRules.referencedScope: AI provider invocation, ProgramKit development capabilities, autonomous registration, ambient permissions, and self-start behavior
referenceRules.rationale: The human initiates provider registration and each authorized use; the tool is not an agent or authority source.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent executable-tool identity, invocation, permissions, provider transport, registration lifecycle, package boundary, and cold-session proof as one validated canonical design.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design grants no executable behavior or registration authority.

valueLifecycle.rationale: The exact canonical bytes are validated, digest-bound by the plan and review manifest, and compared during approved work-unit closure.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The review set is explicit repository input; no agent retrieval contract is created.

agentProcedure.rationale: This design does not create or initialize a capability, skill, MCP server, tool binding, or provider wrapper.

humanCommunication.audience: The human ProgramKit reviewer and later bounded implementer.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only explicit human approval of this review-set version and exact canonical design and plan SHA-256 values authorizes implementation.
humanCommunication.rationale: The Markdown projection, fixtures, validation report, and manifest expose exact identities, boundaries, proof obligations, risks, and deferrals.

governance.provenancePolicy: Exact human intent, ProgramKit b4b14cd source bytes, current official Codex MCP configuration documentation, and stable MCP 2025-11-25 are named; later implementation cannot become design authority.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest and plan bind exact canonical bytes; material changes require revalidation, new digests, and renewed human approval.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Identity, schema, package/executable bytes, operation names, exit codes, access declarations, timeouts, concurrency, idempotency, transport revision, Codex config table, registration lock, package-only boundary, and cold-session protocol version explicitly.
governance.migrationPolicy: Changed contracts or adapters require explicit schema/package revisions and migrations; changed registration requires explicit verified update; incompatible provider drift stops for review.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: Manifests, locks, and evidence include secret reference names and access-policy facts only; inputs, outputs, environment values, credentials, and secret values are excluded.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Canonical documentation remains in ProgramKit or a future owning Development Tool repository; a website may project reviewed content only.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Processes, provider sessions, invocation payloads, and runtime environment state are not durable design content.

artifactDecisions.rationale: A schema-governed design is the review authority while all runtime, adapter, registration, and capability work remains blocked.

security.policy: Access is fail-closed from an exact manifest and independently enforced by the adapter/provider; annotations are descriptive projections only.
guarantees: Filesystem, network, and secrets are denied unless explicitly declared and approved.
Inputs and outputs are schema-validated and exact executable/adapter bytes are verified before advertisement.
exclusions: Tool metadata or model inference never grants permissions.

authority.policy: Only a human starts registration, update, removal, and provider use; the tool and adapter expose no agent or development authority.
guarantees: No self-registration, self-permission, automatic start, capability invocation, provider invocation, or autonomous loop.
Collision and ownership drift refuse mutation.
exclusions: Discovery does not authorize invocation or side effects.

secrets.policy: Only named secret references may be declared; provider-owned secret resolution and redaction remain outside persisted tool evidence.
guarantees: Secret values never enter manifests, locks, command lines, stdout, stderr, or evidence.
exclusions: The first proof permits no secret access.

persistence.policy: Only exact packages, manifests, approved project-scoped registration, ownership lock, and redacted evidence persist.
guarantees: Registration owns one exact TOML table and lock.
exclusions: Invocation process state and conversation state do not persist as tool authority.

failure.policy: Exit codes and structured errors distinguish success, declared failure/cancellation, invocation rejection, and internal fault; timeouts are adapter observations.
guarantees: Invalid identity, schema, permission, package, adapter, collision, or ownership facts fail closed.
No failure is rewritten as success.
exclusions: A host kill has no fabricated tool exit code.

concurrency.policy: The manifest declares positive maximum concurrency and the adapter refuses excess; the first proof allows one active invocation.
guarantees: The adapter does not queue or retry beyond the declared contract.
exclusions: No shared background worker or autonomous scheduler is introduced.

cancellation.policy: MCP cancellation is translated to the child process; the lower contract/provider timeout is enforced; late responses are discarded.
guarantees: Cancellation and timeout evidence are explicit.
Cancellation never claims rollback of side effects.
exclusions: The adapter does not infer compensating behavior.

observability.policy: Evidence binds identities, digests, process/session boundaries, discovery, approval, invocation classification, and redacted result digests.
guarantees: The cold proof records that session A ended and session B discovered solely from persisted registration.
Negative evidence covers tamper, collision, permission, timeout, cancellation, update, and removal.
exclusions: Evidence does not retain secret values or conversational content.

compatibility.policy: Contract, package, executable, adapter, protocol, provider config, schemas, and registration lock version independently and are digest-bound.
guarantees: Incompatible bytes are never silently substituted.
Implementation re-checks authoritative provider sources and stops on material drift.
Consumer builds use exact prepared packages and source mapping only.
exclusions: No compatibility is claimed for provider-native, plugin, remote, or additional-provider transports.

scenarios.intent: Invoke the exact Console proof executable through the provider-neutral contract.
preconditions: Exact local packages, manifest, executable, schemas, and allowed fixture root verify.
steps: Start a fresh proof process with the exact invoke syntax and contract digest.
Write one canonical JSON input to stdin and close it.
Validate exactly one canonical JSON stdout result and exit classification.
Verify declared access, timeout, cancellation, concurrency, idempotency, and evidence.
outcomes: Successful input returns schema-valid output and exit 0.
Identical inputs and exact package bytes produce deterministic proof evidence.
failureOutcomes: Identity, schema, permission, access, or package drift fails before operation behavior.

scenarios.actor: Human reviewer in two isolated Codex sessions
scenarios.intent: Prove provider discovery and invocation solely from explicit persisted registration.
preconditions: Session A has prepared and registered exact approved bytes and then ended completely.
Session B inherits no conversation, path, syntax, process, environment hint, or manual shell instruction.
steps: Start session B in the trusted registered project.
State only the semantic intent to use the registered Console proof.
Observe Codex discover the exact MCP server/tool from persisted configuration.
Approve as required, invoke, validate the structured result, and record evidence.
outcomes: The exact registered tool is discovered and invoked without manual executable knowledge.
Evidence binds both session boundaries and all registered bytes.
failureOutcomes: Inherited state, manual shell instruction, undisclosed executable syntax, or a surviving session-A process invalidates the proof.

scenarios.intent: Register, update, and remove one exact Codex tool without owning unrelated provider configuration.
preconditions: The project is trusted and exact package, manifest, adapter, and provider contract evidence verify.
steps: Refuse server/tool collisions and verify the target table is absent before registration.
Write one exact table and ownership lock, then verify discovery.
Perform an explicit digest-bound update and verify old bytes are rejected.
Perform explicit removal and prove non-discovery in a third cold session.
outcomes: Only owned configuration changes and lifecycle evidence is complete.
failureOutcomes: Missing/tampered adapter, incompatible package, changed owned table, collision, or missing lock refuses mutation.

statusClaims.claim: The review design exists from explicit human intent; no executable contract, Console proof, adapter, registration, capability, or runtime behavior is implemented or approved.
